nodes.title: ITC’s Triple Bottom Line Contribution – Highlights
nodes.summary: The text highlights ITC's Triple Bottom Line contribution across economic, environmental, and social dimensions. Economically, it reports gross revenue of ₹73,465 crore and EBITDA of ₹24,025 crore, ranking among the top three private sector corporates in tax contribution, with future-ready businesses, 25+ mother brands, and 250+ factories. Environmentally, it notes ~52% renewable energy, plastic neutrality since FY22, 17 platinum-certified green buildings, watershed development over 18 lakh acres, afforestation of over 13 lakh acres, climate-smart agriculture on over 31 lakh acres, and 9 Alliance for Water Stewardship platinum sites. Socially, it covers sustainable livelihoods for over 90 lakh women, ITCMAARS with over 20 lakh farmer registrations, maternal and child health support for over 15.2 lakh, education for nearly 22 lakh children, and skilling for over 1.2 lakh youth.

nodes.title: ITC Group – Spanning Agriculture, Manufacturing & Services

Agri Business sources 35 lakh tonnes, supports 20 value chain clusters across 22 states, exports to 95+ countries, and ITCMAARS covers 2,050+ FPOs with 20 lakh+ farmer registrations. Paperboards & Packaging is a leader in value-added paperboards, sustainable plastic substitution, Industry 4.0, and local forestry value chains. ITC Hotels (listed entity) has 140+ hotels in 90+ locations, pioneered 'Responsible Luxury', leads LEED Zero Carbon/Water certifications, and follows an asset-right approach. ITC Infotech, a wholly owned subsidiary, operates in 41 countries and acquired Blazeclan. The text also covers ITC's future-ready FMCG portfolio building core brands and addressing health, nutrition, hygiene, naturals, indulgence, convenience, and sustainability.

nodes.title: THE COMPANY’S GOVERNANCE PHILOSOPHY
nodes.summary: The report outlines ITC Limited's Corporate Governance practices under SEBI Listing Regulations, 2015, emphasizing its formalized system and governance philosophy. It defines corporate governance as a systemic process to enhance wealth-generating capacity while meeting stakeholder aspirations and contributing to the triple bottom line (economic, social, environmental capital). The framework is based on two core principles: executive freedom and effective accountability. From these emerge five cornerstones: trusteeship (protecting shareholder and stakeholder interests), transparency (disclosures and openness), ethical corporate citizenship (exemplary ethical standards), empowerment & accountability (decision-making at appropriate levels with responsibility), and control (checks and balances to prevent misuse of power and manage risks). Each cornerstone is elaborated with its meaning and role in creating the right corporate culture.

nodes.title: THE GOVERNANCE STRUCTURE
nodes.summary: The text describes ITC's three-tier corporate governance structure: strategic supervision by the Board of Directors, strategic management by the Corporate Management Committee, and executive management by the Divisional Chief Executive with the Divisional Management Committee. It explains how this structure ensures objectivity, focused strategic management, and efficient executive management. It outlines that core roles determine responsibilities and formal empowerment, and that the governance structure supports effective management of multiple businesses. It also mentions the availability of the Governance Document on the company website.

nodes.title: ROLES OF VARIOUS ENTITIES
nodes.summary: The text outlines the roles of various entities in ITC's governance. The Board provides trusteeship, strategic supervision, goal-setting, accountability, and annual performance review. Board Committees' roles are set by the Board. The Corporate Management Committee handles strategic management, performance assessment, and resource allocation under Board supervision. Divisional Management Committees manage executive business objectives, with Executive Committees for Business Verticals delivering results. The Chairman is Chief Executive, leads the Board and CMC, and ensures effective functioning. Non-Executive Directors bring independent judgment, Executive Directors assist the Board and lead businesses or functions, and CMC Members contribute to strategic management. Divisional Chief Executives lead day-to-day operations, and Chief Operating Officers lead Vertical Executive Committees to achieve objectives.

nodes.title: Accounting Policies: Investment Property, Impairment, Inventories, and Foreign Currency

Inventories are valued at lower of cost (weighted average, including overheads) and net realisable value, with provisions for obsolete, slow-moving, and defective items. Foreign currency transactions are recorded at transaction-date exchange rates, with settlement and translation gains/losses recognized in profit or loss, while exchange differences on net investment in foreign operations go to other comprehensive income and Foreign Currency Translation Reserve.

nodes.title: Derivatives and Hedge Accounting
nodes.summary: The text covers derivatives and hedge accounting: derivatives are initially recognized at fair value and remeasured each period with gains/losses in profit or loss unless designated as hedging instruments. Hedge accounting requires documentation of relationship, risk management objectives, and strategy. Fair value hedges recognize changes in fair value of hedging instruments and hedged items immediately in profit or loss. Cash flow hedges recognize the effective portion in other comprehensive income as a cash flow hedge reserve, with ineffective portions in profit or loss; amounts are reclassified to profit or loss when the hedged item affects profit or loss, or included in the initial cost of non-financial assets. Hedge accounting is discontinued under specified conditions. Investment in subsidiaries, associates, and joint ventures is carried at cost less impairment. Financial instruments are recognized at fair value or transaction price, with transaction costs added/deducted except for FVTPL. Regular way trades are recognized on trade date. Financial assets are initially recognized at fair value or transaction price, classified based on business model as amortised cost, FVTOCI, or FVTPL, with subsequent measurement rules. Impairment is assessed using expected credit losses, and reclassification occurs only when the business model changes, prospectively without restating prior gains/losses.

nodes.title: 3. Financial risk management objectives

It addresses foreign currency risk with exposures by currency, hedging via forwards, futures, and options, hedge accounting treatment, cash flow hedge reserve movements and recycling timelines, and a foreign currency sensitivity analysis quantifying pre-tax impact on profit and equity.

nodes.title: B. Interest Rate Risk
nodes.summary: The company is virtually debt-free, with deferred payment liabilities not carrying interest, making interest rate risk from financial liabilities negligible. Treasury activities managing debt instrument investments are centralized under approved policies emphasizing safety, liquidity, and returns. Investments are predominantly in Government securities, bonds/debentures, fixed deposits, certificates of deposit, commercial papers, and debt mutual funds. Amortized cost bonds/debentures have temporary mark-to-market movements recouped through coupon accruals. Other bonds/debentures, certificates of deposit, and commercial papers are fair valued through profit and loss to recognize market volatility, deemed insignificant. Fixed deposits are with highly rated banks/companies, short tenure, not subject to interest rate volatility. Debt mutual fund investments face market price risks mainly from interest rate changes impacting return and value, but given the relatively short tenure of underlying portfolios, such price risk is not significant.

nodes.title: Foreign Currency Sensitivity

Interest rate risk: the Group is debt-free with negligible financial liability exposure; investments in government securities, bonds, fixed deposits, certificates of deposit, commercial papers, and debt mutual funds carry insignificant interest rate risk due to short tenures and fair value adjustments. Other price risk: equity investments held for long-term value (₹3632.35 crore in 2025, ₹4676.28 crore in 2024) are measured at fair value through OCI, with commodity futures hedging price risks for agricultural commodities; net exposure is considered insignificant.

nodes.title: Credit Risk

It covers deployment in debt instruments like government securities, fixed deposits, bonds, mutual funds, and commercial papers, with counterparties shortlisted based on credit ratings and financial statements. It reports investments held at amortised cost (₹13,069.90 Crores in 2025 vs ₹14,447.05 Crores in 2024), a large and diverse customer base limiting concentration risk, and payment terms from advance to 180 days credit. Credit is extended per guidelines and policies, with exceptions approved by authorities. No significant financing component exists. Trade receivables are considered a single class due to low and uniform credit risk, with overdue balances evaluated for loss allowances. Trade receivables net of provisions stood at ₹4,719.67 Crores (2025) vs ₹4,025.82 Crores (2024). A table shows the movement in expected loss provision from opening to closing balance, including provisions, utilization, forex effects, and business combination impacts.

nodes.title: Accounting for demerger of Hotels business
nodes.summary: The text covers the accounting for the demerger of ITC's Hotels business into ITC Hotels Limited, approved by NCLT Kolkata on October 4, 2024, with appointed and effective date January 1, 2025. The demerger requires fair value determination involving significant judgments and estimates (future cash flows, growth rate, WACC, discount rates) impacting liability recognition and gains. LSTC - ITC’s Innovation Engine
ITC’s state-of-the-art Life Sciences and Technology Centre (ITC LSTC) in Bengaluru is at the core of driving science- led product innovation to support and build ITC’s portfolio of world-class products and brands. It has completed five decades of industrial research and development (R&D). nodes.title: BRSR Exhibit A: Accounts Payables and Business Openness Metrics

nodes.title: Principle 3
nodes.summary: The text covers Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report disclosures: Principle 3, item 1c on spending for employee and worker well-being (permanent and other-than-permanent) for FY 2023-24 and FY 2024-25 (through 31 December 2024), expressed as a percentage of total revenue (0.4% and 0.3%), with a footnote defining included costs (accident and health insurance, medical reimbursements, maternity and paternity benefits, day-care) and noting that other-than-permanent workers are deployed via service providers who pay their wages and well-being measures. nodes.title: Principle 5
nodes.summary: The text presents data under Principle 5, covering two areas for FY 2024-25 (Apr 1–Dec 31) and FY 2023-24: (1) gross wages paid to females as a percentage of total wages (18% both years), and (2) complaints filed under the POSH Act, including total complaints, complaints as a percentage of female employees/workers, and complaints upheld (1 total, 0.2%, 1 upheld each year). Both sections note the data pertains to permanent employees and workers of the Company.

nodes.title: Principle 6
nodes.summary: Section Principle 6 covers BRSR disclosures: Principle 6 environmental data (energy, water, GHG emissions, waste for FY 2023-24 and part FY 2024-25 with PPP conversion); Principle 8 supply chain sourcing and job creation in smaller towns; and Principle 9 data breaches (nil), plus KPMG's assurance report on BRSR Core disclosures, including opinion, basis, responsibilities, limitations, and exclusions.

nodes.title: Principle 6 (intro)
nodes.summary: The text outlines Principle 6 of a Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report, covering energy, water, greenhouse gas emissions, and waste management disclosures for FY 2023-24 and part of FY 2024-25. It specifies the use of PPP conversion rates aligned with Industry Standards Forum guidance. Energy consumption, renewable percentage, and intensity metrics per rupee of turnover, PPP-adjusted, and per built-up area are detailed. Water consumption and discharge data, including treatment levels, are provided. Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions and their intensities are reported. Waste generation by category, total waste, intensity metrics, and recovery/disposal methods are included, with a note on reclassification of composting waste for FY 2023-24.

nodes.title: Principle 8
nodes.summary: The text presents Principle 8 data for FY 2023-24 and FY 2024-25 (partial). It covers the percentage of input material sourced from suppliers (7.22% and 5.60%), with breakdowns for direct sourcing from MSMEs/small producers and from within India (94.67% and 91.10%). It also discloses job creation in smaller towns, showing wages paid as a percentage of total wage cost across rural, semi-urban, urban, and metropolitan locations (6%, 2%, 28%, 64% for FY 2023-24; 6%, 2%, 29%, 63% for FY 2024-25). A note clarifies the data pertains to permanent employees and workers, and mentions a site reclassification leading to restatement of previous period data.

nodes.title: Principle 9
nodes.summary: Principle 9 of the BRSR requires disclosure of data breach details, here reported as nil, including PII involvement and impact. The section presents ITC Limited's Report and Accounts 2025, featuring KPMG's reasonable assurance report on select BRSR Core sustainability disclosures for 1 April 2024 to 31 March 2025, referencing SEBI regulations, guidance notes, and GHG Protocol. It covers the assurance opinion, basis (ISAE 3000 and 3410), independence, ethics, and quality management. Responsibilities for 'other information' are outlined, excluding BRSR Core, Exhibit-A, and the assurance report. Intended use, management's responsibilities for the ISI (internal controls, reporting criteria, compliance, estimates, fraud prevention), inherent limitations (measurement uncertainty in GHG, water, and energy footprints), auditor's responsibilities (risk-based procedures, testing at 20 locations, reliance on audited financials), and exclusions are also addressed.

nodes.title: Principle 9 (intro)
nodes.summary: The text covers Principle 9 of a Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR), requiring disclosure of data breach details: number of instances (reported as nil), percentage involving personally identifiable information, and impact. It includes part of ITC Limited's Report and Accounts 2025 and an independent practitioners' reasonable assurance report by KPMG Assurance and Consulting Services LLP. The assurance report covers select sustainability disclosures in the BRSR Core Attributes for the period 1 April 2024 to 31 March 2025, referencing SEBI regulations, guidance notes, and GHG Protocol. It outlines the opinion that the identified sustainability information is prepared in accordance with reporting criteria, the basis for opinion citing ISAE 3000 and 3410, independence and ethical compliance, and quality management standards.

nodes.title: Other information
nodes.summary: The text outlines responsibilities for 'other information' in the Company's Report and Accounts 2025, excluding BRSR Core attributes, Exhibit-A, and assurance report. Management and the Board are responsible for this other information, which will be available after the assurance report date. The assurance on BRSR Core does not cover the other information, and no assurance conclusion is expressed on it. The auditor's responsibility is to read the other information when available and consider material inconsistencies with BRSR Core or assurance knowledge, or material misstatements. If a material misstatement is found, it must be communicated to Those Charged With Governance and applicable legal actions described.

nodes.title: Intended use or purpose
nodes.summary:

The ISI and our reasonable assurance report are intended for users who have reasonable knowledge of the BRSR Core attributes including the Exhibit-A to BRSR, the reporting criteria and who have read the information in the ISI with reasonable diligence and understand that the ISI is prepared and assured at appropriate levels of materiality.
Our opinion is not modified in respect of this matter.

nodes.title: Management’s Responsibilities for the Identified Sustainability Information (ISI)
nodes.summary: The text outlines management’s responsibilities for the Identified Sustainability Information (ISI), including designing and maintaining internal controls to prevent material misstatement; selecting and disclosing suitable reporting criteria; preparing, fairly stating, and calculating ISI; ensuring criteria are available to users; establishing targets and implementing actions; providing ownership details; ensuring legal and regulatory compliance; making reasonable judgments and estimates; identifying inherent limitations; preventing and detecting fraud; selecting ISI content and engaging with intended users; informing auditors of other information; and supervising staff. It also notes that Those Charged With Governance oversee the reporting process.

nodes.title: Inherent limitations
nodes.summary:
Inherent limitations
The preparation of the Company’s BRSR information requires the management to establish or interpret the criteria, make determinations about the relevance of information to be included, and make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported information. Measurement of certain amounts and BRSR Core attributes including the Exhibit-A to BRSR metrics, some of which are estimates, is subject to substantial inherent measurement uncertainty, for example, GHG Footprint, Water Footprint, Energy Footprint. Obtaining sufficient appropriate evidence to support our opinion does not reduce the uncertainty in the amounts and metrics.
LVIIBusiness Responsibility and Sustainability Report
REPORT AND ACCOUNTS 2025

nodes.title: Our responsibilities
nodes.summary: The text outlines the auditor's responsibilities for providing reasonable assurance on BRSR Core sustainability disclosures, including planning and performing the engagement, forming an independent opinion, and reporting to the Board. It details the work performed: exercising professional judgment and skepticism, designing procedures based on risk assessment of material misstatement, understanding internal controls, and assessing criteria suitability, reporting policies, quantification methods, and estimates. Procedures included substantive testing at 20 operational locations and reliance on audited standalone financial statements for specified financial data, culminating in an evaluation of overall presentation.

It excludes the Company's strategy statements, progress on goals (beyond assured scope), opinions, claims, beliefs, aspirations, expectations, future intentions, intellectual property assertions, and competitive issues. nodes.title: Annexure – 1
nodes.summary: Annexure 1 of ITC Limited's BRSR Core Attributes outlines nine areas: fairness in engaging with customers and suppliers, open-ness of business, employee wellbeing and safety, gender diversity, energy footprint, water footprint, GHG footprint, circularity (waste), and inclusive development. It lists parameters for each, including accounts payable days, purchase/sales concentration, related party transactions, employee wellbeing spending, safety incidents, female wage share, sexual harassment complaints, energy consumption and intensity, water withdrawal, consumption, intensity and discharge, Scope 1 and 2 emissions and intensity, waste generation, recovery and disposal by category and intensity, input sourcing from MSMEs/small suppliers and within India, wages in smaller towns, and customer data breach instances.

nodes.title: Orbit Next: Accelerating Growth
nodes.summary: ITC Infotech achieved top-quartile FY 2024-25 performance through strategic initiatives focused on Customer Centricity, Employee Centricity, and Operational Excellence, advancing its Orbit Next journey. It secured high-impact transformation programs and deepened key client relationships. The company leveraged AI to launch GenAI platforms OmniFabrik and K-Fabrik, opened a Global AI Center of Excellence in Kolkata, and trained over 9,000 employees in AI. It expanded global presence across the Americas, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia Pacific, opened a subsidiary in Saudi Arabia, and acquired Blazeclan Technologies to deepen reach in Southeast Asia and ANZ markets.

nodes.title: Reinforcement of our Commitment to Sustainability
nodes.summary:
Reinforcement of our Commitment to Sustainability
A key component of the Company’s Orbit Next strategy is developing differentiated capabilities and solutions. In line with the strategic intent, ITC Infotech entered into a definitive agreement to acquire 100% shareholding of Blazeclan Technologies Private Limited - a leading Cloud consulting firm with deep expertise across Hyperscalers and strong data platform capabilities. This acquisition enabled the company to deliver comprehensive, end-to-end solutions across multi-cloud and hybrid cloud environments. It serves as a critical enabler to drive accelerated digital transformation for clients and reinforces ITC Infotech’s position as a trusted partner in their cloud and AI first journeys.

nodes.title: Empowering People to Drive Strategic Growth
nodes.summary: The text covers two main areas. First, it details the company's people strategy under its Orbit Next strategy, including investments in talent attraction, development, and retention, with FY 2024-25 initiatives such as bespoke learning pathways, upskilling, leadership programs, employee listening, and transparent communication, leading to stronger engagement and retention. Second, it describes the Sustainability programme's FY 2024-25 achievements: planting 18,000 saplings with a 90% survival rate, constructing two rainwater harvesting units, rejuvenating a 4-acre urban lake, and 262 employees volunteering 1,362 hours in environmental activities. It also includes the heading 'Creating Enduring Institutions' and a report reference.

nodes.title: CII-ITC Centre of Excellence for Sustainable Development
key_items: Building Climate Resilience and Low Carbon Economy; Facilitating an Enabling Ecosystem for ESG; Nature Positive Actions
Building Climate Resilience and Low Carbon Economy
Facilitating an Enabling Ecosystem for ESG
nodes.summary: The CII-ITC Centre of Excellence for Sustainable Development (CESD), established in 2006 to promote the Triple Bottom Line philosophy, highlights its activities: building climate resilience and a low carbon economy through the CII Climate Action Charter with over 500 signatories, participation in COP29 with a report on Indian industry expectations, a collaboration with CEEW on a Physical Climate Risk Assessment Framework, and contribution to India's National Inventory of Greenhouse Gases for the IPPU sector under NATCOM; facilitating an enabling ESG ecosystem by forming a Core Group for SEBI's Industry Standards Forum to develop BRSR Core reporting standards, with CII's recommendations accepted by SEBI; and nature positive actions via the India Business and Biodiversity Initiative's participation in consultations for updating the National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan and adopting National Biodiversity Targets.

nodes.title: ITC Sangeet Research Academy
nodes.summary: The ITC Sangeet Research Academy (ITC SRA), established by ITC in 1977, is a Public Charitable Trust dedicated to preserving, propagating, and teaching Hindustani classical music through the Guru-Shishya Parampara. It aims to create future masters, offering full scholarships to handpicked students who train under eminent Gurus like Pandit Ajoy Chakrabarty and Pandit Ulhas Kashalkar. The academy's scholars receive national scholarships and perform at events like the ITC Sangeet Sammelan and Mini Sangeet Sammelans across India. Recent initiatives include a special Independence Day piece 'Desh Ek Raag' and its first Thumri Festival in March 2025. The text also notes Pandit Uday Bhawalkar's Rashtriya Kalidas Samman and ITC SRA's role in upholding national heritage.

nodes.title: Major Awards & Certifications 2024-2025
nodes.summary: The text lists major awards and certifications from 2024-2025 for ITC and its executives. Chairman & Managing Director Sanjiv Puri received the AIMA JRD Tata Corporate Leadership Award, Sir Jehangir Ghandy Medal, and Fortune India Best CEO in Diversified Conglomerate. CFO Supratim Dutta won Group CFO of the Year at ET CFO Awards 2025. ITC ranked 1st in Conglomerates in BW Businessworld's Most Sustainable Companies, won India's Top Value Creator from Dun & Bradstreet, Platinum at FICCI Sustainable Industrial Practice Awards, IIT Madras CSR Award for Climate Smart Agriculture, first prize at BRICS Industrial Innovation Contest for PSPD, Asia-Pacific Gartner Eye on Innovation Awards for PSPD, WorldStar and AsiaStar awards for Packaging & Printing, FICCI Sustainable Agriculture Award, Gold at Financial Express Green Sarathi Awards for Water Stewardship, Platinum at CII Industry-Academia Partnership Awards for ITCMAARS, and multiple SABRE Asia-Pacific Awards for FMCG businesses including Matches & Agarbatti, Personal Care, and Foods.

nodes.title: Major Awards & Certifications over the Years
nodes.summary: The text lists major awards and certifications received by ITC and its Chairman & Managing Director, Mr. Sanjiv Puri. It covers individual honors for Mr. Puri, including Business Leader of the Year, Best CEO, Transformational Leader Award, Distinguished Alumnus Award, and ranking among India's Most Valuable CEOs. ITC's awards include the Global Kaizen Award, Best Industry for CSR Activities, Best Governed Company, Porter Prize, World Business and Development Award, and Cannes Lions awards for Savlon. nodes.title: ITC Limited
key_items: NOTICE OF 114 TH ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING
nodes.summary: This notice convenes ITC Limited's 114th Annual General Meeting on 25 July 2025 via video conferencing. Ordinary business includes adopting financial statements for FY2024-25, confirming interim dividend of ₹6.50 and declaring final dividend of ₹7.85 per share, re-appointing directors Hemant Malik and Atul Singh, approving auditor remuneration up to ₹4.40 crore for FY2025-26, and ratifying cost auditors' remuneration for specific products. Special business includes re-appointing Shyamal Mukherjee as Independent Director, appointing secretarial auditors for five years, and approving related-party transactions with BAT GLP up to ₹2,350 crore for FY2026-27 and ITC Filtrona up to ₹1,100 crore for FY2025-26. The record date for final dividend is 28 May 2025, with payment between 28-31 July 2025.

S. N. nodes.title: Item No. 6
nodes.summary: This explanatory statement concerns the re-appointment of Mr. Shyamal Mukherjee as an Independent Director for five years. It notes his original appointment in 2021, the Board's recommendation based on the Nomination & Compensation Committee's advice, and his consent, notice, and declaration of independence under the Companies Act, 2013 and SEBI Listing Regulations. The Committee and Board endorse his skills, experience, and contributions, confirming he meets all regulatory requirements. Remuneration includes sitting fees, accident insurance, and a commission of ₹1–1.3 crore annually. Additional information is referenced in the Directors' Report and Corporate Governance Report. His shareholding (21,000 Ordinary Shares) is disclosed, and he and his relatives are interested in the resolution, while other Directors and Key Managerial Personnel are not. The Board recommends the Special Resolution for approval.

nodes.title: Item No. 7

Ananthasubramanian & Co. as Secretarial Auditors for five financial years starting 2025-26, subject to member approval. The Board, on Audit Committee recommendation, proposed member approval for these transactions. nodes.title: Nature of the proposed transaction
nodes.summary: The text outlines proposed related-party transactions: sale of Indian unmanufactured tobacco and purchase of international unmanufactured tobacco (including storage/holding) with BAT GLP, capped at ₹2,350 Crores for FY 2026-27, pricing benchmarked to unrelated party transactions, with contracts spanning multiple years. It also covers purchase of filter rods/tube filters and sale of capsules/flavours with IFL (a joint venture of GFCL and Filtrona), up to ₹1,100 Crores for FY 2025-26, similarly benchmarked. Each transaction's percentage of consolidated turnover (2.9% and 1.4% for BAT GLP and IFL, respectively), justifications (business growth, company experience, IFL's expertise), absence of valuation reports, director/KMP interest, voting restrictions for related parties, and board recommendation for approval are detailed.
